analysis: Both units are head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines ~800-1253), documentation of historical release entries for v0.9.12-v0.9.18 and unreleased-adjacent items. The PR diff for this file is a documentation restructure (the new v0.10.0 candidate section and reordering); no executable code, configuration, or security control changed in the supplied evidence. I read the entries for threat-model-relevant claims: SSD prefix-cache write-endurance ledger and encrypted checkpoints (T-041, SEC-035), frozen legacy MDM cohort and App Attest gating (TB-011, T-052/T-053/T-054/T-057), account erasure, coordinator log PII removal, and provider-bound body field stripping. These statements are descriptive and consistent with the retained threat model. They do not loosen the 30-minute TTL, authenticated account scoping, HMAC-keyed names, or the App Attest authorization requirements. The only concern would be that the changelog misstates a control, but that is not a security regression and is not provable without the source. Remaining uncertainty: the head text only shows part of the patch; the v0.10.0 section (lines 6-662) was not supplied in these units, including claims about prompt normalization v9, MLX kernel bumps, and new model registration gating, so those cross-version rollout claims and any threat-model update needs (for example, cache scope mismatch behavior across v8/v9) should be examined where that text is supplied. No findings are made on the supplied lines.
